## Why this file is here

`tools/era_runtime_probe.py` identifies the ROM's build environment by
assembling the era toolchains' hand-written Thumb runtime routines and comparing
the bytes against `baserom.gba`. It reads exactly one file per candidate tree.
Two candidates exist:

- **`agbcc`** — the tree `make toolchain` provisions from the pinned
  `pret/agbcc` commit.
- **`gcc-2.95.3`** — vanilla GCC 2.95.3, kept as the comparison baseline.

The baseline matters for two separate reasons, and both are satisfied by this
one file:

1. The five routine rows for `gcc-2.95.3` are assembled from it.
2. The probe's **negative control** lives only in this file. Vanilla GCC 2.95.3
   ships a mode-switching interworking veneer (`L_interwork_call_via_rX`,
   lines 669-747) that agbcc replaced with a plain `bx rN` stub, and agbcc's own
   `lib1thumb.asm` does not contain that macro at all — it ends after
   `L_call_via_rX`. Earlier setups took the file from a full 12.9 MB GCC source
   tree, none of which the probe ever read. Vendoring the single file
   makes `make matching-ready` reproducible on a machine with no GCC 2.95.3
   checkout, and removes the last un-provisionable input from the gate.

Do not edit this file. If a newer or differently-sourced copy is ever needed,
replace it whole, keep the upstream notice, and update the SHA-256 above in the
same change — `tools/era_runtime_probe.py` compares its own output against the
recorded `docs/data/era_runtime_probe.json`, so a changed file that still
matches the ROM is the only acceptable reason for that hash to move.

## Provenance caveat

The copy here was taken from the local GCC 2.95.3 tree that was in hand when the
runtime-provenance evidence was recorded (`docs/data/era_runtime_probe.json`),
not re-downloaded from `ftp.gnu.org`. Its content is the FSF file described
above; the recorded probe rows reproduce byte-for-byte from it, which is
independent evidence that it is the same file the evidence was measured with.
Reconciling it against the published GCC 2.95.3 release tarball has not been
done and would be a welcome contribution.
